title: Turn off Licensing
summary: The requirement cascade on Diceroll's Features page: turning off Licensing also turns off Commerce, which needs it. The dialog names every dependent with what stops for each, says what is kept, and shows the one audited change it will record in Activity.
compare: The dialog opens over the Features page (dimmed, drawn as products.features) when the Licensing switch is pressed and before anything changes; Escape and Cancel leave both features on. With the dialog open the page can't scroll: on desktop the dialog is centred in the viewport (ui/Dialog.tsx).
The title names the feature and the product: 'Turn off Licensing for Diceroll?'. The lead line says why more turns off: 'Commerce needs Licensing, so it turns off too, in the same change.'

Every feature that turns off is listed, the one pressed first and then each dependent (transitively), each with its glyph, 'On → Off' and one sentence on what stops. A dependent carries 'Needs Licensing'. Features that are already off (Cloud Sync) are not listed.

The Licensing line says what players experience, from the SDK gate's offline grace: players already activated keep playing until their offline window ends (up to 30 days); after that, and on every new install, Diceroll can't confirm a license, Free tier included. Then the reach in real numbers from the dry run: devices that checked a license in the last 30 days (11,239).
The Commerce line says what players notice: the game can't show the 4 offers or confirm a purchase, so in-game buying stops and restores are refused.

What is kept is said plainly (licenses, tiers, offers and purchases), then one sentence on coming back: turning Licensing back on with its switch leaves Commerce off; reverting this change in Activity turns both back on.
'In Activity, as one change' previews the single audit entry with the actor (Ada Lindqvist), 'Settings → Features · one entry for both'. One entry, not two.

The danger button says exactly what happens: 'Turn off Licensing and Commerce'. No typed confirmation. Cancel is the neutral outline button (visible in dark) and has focus when the dialog opens (EXPERIENCE.md confirmations).
The words are feature names only; no service slugs (license, commerce) and no 'capability'.

Phone: the dialog is the console's bottom sheet (rounded top corners, drag handle, safe-area padding at the foot), the danger button full width above Cancel, and the 'On → Off' marks stay on each feature's title line.

Pressed, the danger button reads 'Turning off…' with a spinner and both buttons are disabled. If it fails the dialog stays open with an inline error saying what went wrong and how to retry, and both features stay on (ADMIN.md §5.2).
This is a danger dialog because a dependent turns off and it reaches many devices; turning off a feature that nothing needs is a caution dialog (L1) with its consequences.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the Licensing line now says what players experience, the dialog is centred on desktop and a bottom sheet on phone, and Cancel is visible in dark.

findings.issue: The Licensing line said the game can't activate or refresh a license but never said what players experience: whether activated copies keep running offline, for how long, and whether Free-tier players are locked out.
findings.resolution: Rewritten from the SDK gate's offline grace (client-core gate.ts runs a cached license until graceUntil): 'Players already activated keep playing until their offline window ends, up to 30 days. After that, and on every new install, Diceroll can't confirm a license, Free tier included.' The 11,239 reach figure stays.

findings.issue: On phone the dialog was a top-anchored card, not the console's bottom sheet; on desktop it was top-anchored rather than centred; in dark Cancel's fill matched the dialog surface.
findings.resolution: With the dialog open the page no longer scrolls, so the render is the first viewport: centred on desktop, a bottom sheet on phone (rounded top corners, drag handle, safe-area padding, danger above Cancel). Cancel is an outline button. Lead: the kit's .overlay still top-anchors every dialog; a kit-wide sheet and centring would spare each screen this override.

findings.issue: 'Turning Licensing back on later doesn't turn Commerce back on' and 'Reverting this change turns both back on' read as contradicting each other; no busy or failure state; initial focus not stated.
findings.resolution: One sentence now: 'Turning Licensing back on with its switch leaves Commerce off; reverting this change in Activity turns both back on.' The audit meta says 'one entry for both'. Compare adds the busy label 'Turning off…', the inline error that keeps both features on, and initial focus on Cancel (shown focused in the render).

findings.issue: Cross-screen: the Features page under the dialog had per-service switch colours and 20 px phone switches.
findings.resolution: The page underneath follows products.features: console-accent switches, Packages, requirement marks, 44×24 switches on phone.
